title: Energy modeling specialist
description:
You are a building energy modeling specialist. You have 3 to 7 years of hands-on experience running full building energy simulations and you know the difference between a well-built model and a model that simply runs. You take modeling seriously and your work product reflects it. 



You are an IES VE expert. IES Virtual Environment is your primary simulation tool. You know it deeply: you can build geometry from scratch, assign constructions, configure HVAC systems, set up occupancy and lighting profiles, run compliance checks, and interpret results. You do not need to be trained on IES VE. 



You know ASHRAE 90.1-2022 inside and out. You have applied both the Energy Cost Budget (ECB) method and the Performance Rating Method (PRM) on real projects. You understand the mandatory requirements, prescriptive path, and how the compliance pathways differ and when each applies. 



You are proficient in the 2024 IECC. You understand the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code commercial provisions including the mandatory requirements, prescriptive compliance path, and Energy Rating Index (ERI) compliance options. You can navigate Section C401 through C408 without looking everything up. 



You understand building systems at a technical level. Envelope assemblies, U-values, SHGC, infiltration rates, HVAC system types and efficiencies, lighting power densities, and plug loads are part of your everyday vocabulary. You know how modeling assumptions affect results. 



You are a strong communicator. You write and speak English at a professional level. You can explain complex energy model results to engineers, architects, and clients in a way that is accurate and understandable. This is a requirement, not a preference. 



You are detail-oriented and self-directed. You catch your own errors before they become client-facing problems. You manage your time, meet deadlines, and produce deliverables that do not require extensive rework. 



 



WHAT YOU WILL DO 



Perform complete building energy simulations using IES VE for new construction, major renovation, and retrofit projects across multiple building types including Healthcare, Mission Critical, Higher Education, and Government facilities. 



Conduct ASHRAE 90.1-2022 compliance modeling using both the Energy Cost Budget (ECB) method and the Performance Rating Method (PRM). Document the baseline building configuration, proposed design, and performance results in accordance with the standard. 



Perform 2024 IECC commercial energy compliance analysis including mandatory requirements review, prescriptive path compliance verification, and trade-off calculations. Produce compliance documentation suitable for submittal to authorities having jurisdiction (AHJ). 



Model all major building systems within IES VE including building envelope assemblies (walls, roofs, floors, fenestration), HVAC systems (air-side and water-side), domestic hot water, lighting systems, plug loads, and on-site renewable energy where applicable. 



Evaluate energy conservation measures (ECMs) through parametric modeling. Run multiple design scenarios, compare results, and provide clear recommendations with supporting data to help clients and design teams make informed decisions. 



Collaborate with commissioning engineers to compare modeled system performance against installed equipment schedules and sequences of operation. Identify discrepancies and support the commissioning process with energy-based analysis. 



Coordinate with project architects and MEP engineers of record to obtain accurate model inputs including construction assemblies, equipment schedules, ventilation rates, and occupancy data. Document all assumptions clearly and maintain an assumption log for each project. 



Prepare clear, professional energy model reports documenting methodology, inputs, results, and conclusions. Reports must be suitable for client delivery and regulatory submittal. 



Support Building Envelope Commissioning (BECx) efforts with thermal bridging analysis, condensation risk review, and energy impact assessment of envelope performance gaps. 



Stay current with code updates, standard revisions, and software developments. As ASHRAE standards and energy codes evolve, you will be expected to adapt modeling practices accordingly. 



 



POSITION REQUIREMENTS 



Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Building Science, or a closely related field (required) 



3 to 7 years of hands-on building energy modeling experience on real construction projects (required) 



Proficiency in IES Virtual Environment (IES VE) is required and nonnegotiable. Candidates who do not have demonstrated IES VE experience will not be considered. 



INTERVIEW REQUIREMENT: All candidates must present a minimum of two completed IES VE energy models during the interview. Candidates will be expected to walk through their modeling approach, explain key assumptions, identify compliance outcomes, and answer detailed technical questions about the models. Presenting borrowed or template models is grounds for immediate disqualification. 



POSITION REQUIREMENTS 

-Demonstrated proficiency in ASHRAE 90.1-2022 including ECB method, PRM compliance pathway, mandatory provisions, and envelope and mechanical system requirements 

-Demonstrated proficiency in 2024 IECC commercial energy provisions including mandatory requirements, prescriptive compliance, and trade-off compliance paths 

-Familiarity with EnergyPlus or DOE-2 simulation engines is a plus 

-Exceptional English proficiency, written and verbal, at a professional business level (required, nonnegotiable) 

-Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite including Word, Excel, and Outlook 

-Must be available to work hours that overlap with US Central Time (CST) business hours on a consistent, daily basis 

-Full time position, minimum 40 hours per week

You'll be using Claude (or ChatGPT) to write the actual customer responses. s

s, one for ad comments. When an
 or comment comes in, you just paste it into the chat — and in most cases, the AI will write the full response without you having to explain anything. Prior experience using Claude or ChatGPT for customer support — ideally for an e-commerce brand. You don't need to be an AI expert, but you should have some experience working with AI tools in a support workflow

Strong English reading comprehension — you don't need to write fluent English from scratch yourself (the AI handles the writing), but you need to fully understand customer messages, know what they're asking, and understand what the AI is generating so you can spot anything off

 account

Reliable and responsive

s and comments is much faster and more efficient than traditional support. Once you've gotten the hang of the task and set up your AI properly, the work goes very quickly.
